obstacles: Wild lifespan is harder to measure than captive lifespan.
As a rule needs a chosen population proportion.
rationale: Cephalopod lifespan and post-reproductive senescence are standard life-history variables with extensive records. Existing data can resolve both the typical lifespan and female decline.

operationalization: Analyze surface video of Argonauta argo in wind, tracking web deployment, arm position and movement relative to wind and current. Wind-driven acceleration with web deployment supports sailing; submerged propulsion refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: argonaut morphology, ecology and behavior references

candidate_datasets.name: OBIS
candidate_datasets.role: georeferenced argonaut observations

obstacles: Rare offshore surface behavior has little systematic video.
Currents confound apparent wind propulsion.
rationale: The mechanical prediction is clear and existing observations can assess arm and web use. Public data are too sparse and uncontrolled for a comprehensive hydrodynamic test.

operationalization: Use developmental and anatomical imaging to locate silk glands and spinnerets, determine whether hatchlings produce silk, and trace thread material from internal glands to body surface. Internal gland origin refutes the bark-like mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public spider anatomical specimens and scans

obstacles: Off the body could merely describe the visible exit point rather than material origin.
rationale: Spider silk anatomy and juvenile spinning are extensively documented and directly observable. Modern imaging cleanly discriminates external shedding from secretion by internal glands.

operationalization: Track individually marked honey bees for complete foraging bouts and identify each visited plant taxon by video, pollen or DNA. Any mixed-species trip refutes the absolute claim; the proportion of flower-constant trips tests its typical form.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: bee-plant visitation interaction records

obstacles: Most visitation datasets do not retain trip-level sequences.
Flower identification from mixed pollen can be imperfect.
rationale: Flower constancy is a standard measurable behavior with substantial experimental literature. Existing open interaction data lack complete trip structure, so universality is only partly resolvable without targeted raw records.

operationalization: From hive videos and colony records, quantify queen killing and royal-cell destruction relative to queen number and impending swarming. Increased destruction when no swarm occurs supports regulation, but not workers' stated fear.
obstacles: Aristotle's kings must be mapped to queens.
Fear and intent are not directly measurable.
Hive-management practices alter queen replacement.
rationale: Queen elimination and cell destruction are observable and can be related to colony fission. Existing records can test the behavioral association, while the intentional explanation remains underdetermined.

operationalization: Record sting retention, tissue avulsion and survival after honey-bee workers sting substrates of differing elasticity. Death associated with a retained barbed sting and abdominal rupture supports the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public insect anatomical imaging relevant to sting morphology

obstacles: Bees can sometimes withdraw stings from other insects and survive.
rationale: The anatomy, injury and survival outcome are directly observable and extensively documented. Existing evidence can also resolve the scope conditions under which the claim holds.

operationalization: Age-mark worker bees and record task allocation and hair wear through life. Age-related shifts toward or away from foraging, plus measured setal abrasion, directly test each clause.
obstacles: Hairiness may reflect wear rather than indoor exposure.
Colony needs can reverse normal age polyethism.
rationale: Worker age and task are standard variables in honey-bee experiments with abundant existing data. The direction stated is sharply testable, as is the proposed morphology association.

operationalization: Video-record bees departing in high versus low wind and identify any deliberately carried stones, then measure flight stability with and without ballast. Repeated high-wind flights without stones refute the generalization.
obstacles: No known public dataset records carried-object identity and wind simultaneously.
Pollen or debris could be mistaken for stones.
rationale: The prediction is unusually concrete and highly discriminable, but ordinary bee datasets do not measure it. A decisive assessment needs new high-speed field observations.

operationalization: Mark workers and queens in Vespula and Polistes colonies and estimate overwinter survival and refuges. Worker survival into spring refutes the universal worker-death clause; queen recovery underground supports overwintering.

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: seasonally dated social-wasp occurrence records

obstacles: Polistes and Vespula differ in colony cycle.
Winter non-detection alone does not prove death.
rationale: Social-wasp colony cycles and caste survival are standard, well-studied life-history outcomes. Existing observations and experiments can resolve the main claim across the named genera.

operationalization: For identified lions involved in livestock or human attacks, compare age, dental condition and hunting performance with non-conflict lions. Enrichment of old, dentally impaired individuals supports the proposed pathway.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open lion movement data that can characterize livestock-area incursions

obstacles: Attack databases rarely include dental exams.
Habitat loss, prey depletion and opportunity confound age effects.
rationale: Attack, age and tooth condition are measurable, and some case series exist. Public linked records are incomplete and observational confounding prevents a clean universal causal conclusion.

operationalization: Analyze elephant swimming observations and respiratory anatomy, testing whether submerged animals keep the trunk tip in air and move air through it. Trunk occlusion or alternative breathing would refute the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public elephant anatomical imaging

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public wildlife video of elephant aquatic behavior

rationale: The anatomical airway and snorkeling behavior are directly visible and extensively documented. Existing images, videos and anatomy provide a decisive test.

operationalization: Follow hens before and after winning fights against cocks, measuring crowing, mounting, comb and tail morphology and spur growth, while recording age and ovarian status. Trait changes specifically following victory support the claim.
obstacles: Hormonal aging or ovarian disease can masculinize hens independently of fighting.
Public longitudinal fight-linked data are scarce.
rationale: All phenotypes are measurable, and existing poultry reports can test their occurrence. The asserted causal trigger is strongly confounded and lacks adequate public longitudinal data.

operationalization: Compare castrated and intact cocks by age at procedure for comb color, crowing, mating and male-trait development. Consistent loss or prevention after verified gonadal ablation supports the claim.
obstacles: Cauterizing the rump may not reliably castrate birds.
Historical procedure differs from modern caponization.
Open individual-level datasets are limited.
rationale: Androgen-dependent traits are explicit and many poultry experiments exist. The exact described intervention is ambiguous, so current data resolve hormonal castration better than cauterization itself.

operationalization: Compare voice pitch, androgen-dependent hair and baldness in men with documented prepubertal castration versus matched intact men. Any later hair, voice lowering or baldness refutes the corresponding absolute.
obstacles: Relevant historical cohorts are small and sensitive.
Age at castration and hormone treatment are often undocumented.
Never goes bald requires long follow-up.
rationale: The phenotypes are standard clinical variables and historical eunuch cohorts provide evidence. Public individual-level data are limited, and modern hormone treatment complicates a definitive universal test.

operationalization: Follow stags castrated before and after antler growth, recording antler initiation, size and annual casting against intact controls. Any antler growth after early castration or shedding after late castration refutes the absolutes.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public deer skeletal morphology records

obstacles: Castration timing and longitudinal antler histories are rarely open.
Antler response depends on season relative to the testosterone cycle.
rationale: The intervention and outcomes are precise, and veterinary or deer-farm studies provide partial evidence. Existing open data likely do not cover enough timing conditions for the full prediction.

operationalization: Code rumination and upper-incisor presence across mammal species and calculate their association and exceptions. Ruminants with upper incisors or non-ruminants lacking them determine the limits of the rule.

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open comparative animal traits and source references

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public skull and dentition scans

obstacles: A few acknowledged exceptions make the exact decision threshold important.
rationale: Dentition and rumination are standard species traits with broad comparative coverage. Public anatomy and natural-history records permit a straightforward phylogenetic contingency analysis.

operationalization: Compare season-dated photographs and recordings within bird species for plumage color and song features. Repeatable within-individual or population seasonal shifts support the general claim; the blackbird example can be assessed separately.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: season-dated bird photographs, video and audio

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: seasonal bird observation records with media links

obstacles: Age and molt can be confounded with season.
The historical owsel may not map exactly to Turdus merula.
rationale: Large public media archives contain the needed dates, colors and vocalizations. Standard image and acoustic analyses can test many species and the stated example.

operationalization: Compare morphology, genomes, banded individuals and seasonal occurrences of robin versus redstart and garden warbler versus blackcap. Distinct genomes and simultaneous populations refute seasonal transformation.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public sequence data for the four bird species

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: georeferenced and dated occurrences

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: public DNA barcode records

obstacles: Ancient names must be mapped carefully, though the proposed modern pairs are explicit.
rationale: Species identity and seasonal presence are exceptionally well covered by genetic and occurrence data. Multiple independent analyses decisively distinguish transformation from separate migratory species.

operationalization: Code dust- and water-bathing events by species, locomotor ecology, habitat and talon morphology from public videos and species accounts. Counterexamples test each categorical association.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public bird bathing-behavior media

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: species habitat occurrences and media-linked observations

obstacles: Absence of bathing in media is not evidence of absence.
Crooked versus straight talons needs a morphological rule.
rationale: Positive bathing observations are plentiful and can refute universal exclusions. Systematic behavior coverage across the broad bird groups is incomplete, limiting confirmation.

operationalization: No observation can rank final cause as metaphysically prior to motor cause without first adopting Aristotle's causal framework.
obstacles: Priority among kinds of cause is a conceptual claim.
No unique measurable consequence distinguishes it from rival causal vocabularies.
rationale: This is a methodological and metaphysical ordering of explanations, not a biological prediction. Scientific datasets can describe mechanisms and functions but cannot settle the asserted ontological priority.

operationalization: Use embryological time series to determine whether vertebrae arise by patterned segmentation before fetal contortion or by fracture of a continuous backbone. Observed somitic segmentation without breakage refutes Empedocles' mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: EMAGE: Edinburgh Mouse Atlas of Gene Expression
candidate_datasets.role: public mouse embryo spatial-development data

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public vertebrate embryological and anatomical imaging

obstacles: The broader denial that animal characters are incidental is too sweeping, but the vertebral example is direct.
rationale: Modern embryology records the temporal origin of vertebral segmentation and sharply discriminates patterned development from accidental breakage. Existing imaging resolves the stated example directly.

operationalization: Estimate parent-offspring resemblance and genetic transmission for specified traits using pedigrees and genomes, while separating inherited from environmental effects. Heritable resemblance supports the claim; no parental predictive contribution would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public genomic sequences across animals

candidate_datasets.name: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public genotype-trait association data, especially in humans

obstacles: Certain characters is unspecified.
Parent phenotype alone does not establish a developmental mechanism.
rationale: Inheritance and parent-offspring resemblance are represented by enormous public genomic and pedigree resources. The general wording is broad, but many explicit trait operationalizations can directly test its core.

operationalization: Locomotion can be measured, but 'intellect' has no species-neutral operational definition that preserves the categorical claim; cognitive task performance tests narrower abilities only.
obstacles: Intellect is undefined and anthropocentric.
No finite behavioral battery establishes absence of intellect.
Different cognitive capacities yield conflicting classifications.
rationale: Animal cognition datasets can compare memory, planning or problem solving, but none resolve the philosophical category asserted here. The human-only boundary changes with the chosen proxy, so the claim as stated lacks a discriminating empirical criterion.

operationalization: Measure respiratory airflow, core and respiratory-tract temperature and heat exchange through breathing cycles across air-breathing animals. If airflow persists without the predicted heat alternation or is driven by pressure-generating muscles and gas demand, the stated necessary mechanism is refuted.

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open metabolic-rate measurements and source references across terrestrial animals

obstacles: Heat discharge may be an effect of ventilation rather than its driver.
Coverage is richer for mammals and birds than other air breathers.
rationale: Respiratory mechanics, temperature and metabolism are standard physiological measurements with extensive public records. Temporal and intervention evidence can distinguish thermal driving from rival muscular and chemical-control mechanisms.

operationalization: Code wings and flight behavior across ant species and castes. Verified winged flying reproductives and wingless workers within ants directly confirm that the group spans both categories.

candidate_datasets.name: AntWeb
candidate_datasets.role: public ant specimen images, taxonomy and caste records

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: public ant occurrence and specimen records

obstacles: Flight status differs mainly by caste and life stage rather than species.
rationale: Winged reproductive ants and wingless workers are directly documented in extensive public collections. The classification point is decisively testable with standard morphology and observation.
